mpRateNote: Monetary Policy Rate cut 250bps to 10.75% at the 30 September 2026 MPC (from 13.25%), the lowest in several years, as inflation eased back inside the BoZ target band. Prior path: 13.25% held at the August 2026 MPC (26 Aug); 25bps cut from 13.50% at the May 2026 MPC; 75bps cut from 14.25% on 11 Feb 2026. The 30 Sep decision coincided with the 10% copper-concentrate export duty taking effect and the start of IMF successor-programme talks.

trendAnalysis.outlook: The kwacha is flat-lining rather than trending. The USD/ZMW market mid sits at ~K20.26 (open.er-api.com, 4 Nov) versus ~K20.27 on 30 Oct — effectively unchanged — while the BoZ official fix edged from 20.201 (30 Oct) to 20.239 (3 Nov), a modest 0.19% softening. The basket is mixed: sterling (+0.48%) and the euro (+0.28%) cost slightly more kwacha, while the yuan (-0.70%) and pula (-0.58%) cost less, pointing to cross-currency noise rather than one-way kwacha selling. Support still comes from record copper output and export earnings, reserves near US$5.5bn, a near-complete debt restructuring and the US$1.47bn IMF staff-level agreement. The offset is a materially easier policy stance after the 30 September 2026 MPC cut the MPR 250bps to 10.75% with inflation back inside the 6-8% band, plus the 10% copper-concentrate export duty that took effect the same day. Watch copper prices, month-start corporate USD demand and the pace of further BoZ easing.
trendAnalysis.projection3m: USD/ZMW 19.20–20.50 range. Post-election policy continuity and IMF talks supportive; softer policy rate, import demand and copper-price swings the main risks.
trendAnalysis.projection6m: USD/ZMW 18.50–20.50 range. Direction hinges on fiscal continuity, copper earnings and the pace of further BoZ easing.
